newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Tajik rebels agree to free foreign hostages - govt.
newsitem.headline: Tajik rebels agree to free foreign hostages - govt.

text.p: The Tajik government said on Saturday that seven United Nations military observers and 15 other hostages seized by rebels would be freed later in the day.

Amirkul Azimov, Secretary of Tajikistan's Security Council, told Reuters the rebels, who say they are loyal to rebel field commander Rizvon Sadirov, had agreed to release all 22 hostages after talks with government representatives which lasted through the night.

He gave no details of terms, if any, for their release and did not specify when or where the would be freed. U.N. sources said two of the military observers were Bulgarian and others came from Denmark, Jordan, Ukraine, Uruguay and Austria.
The rebel group had earlier threatened to kill the hostages, seized on Friday, and detonate 30 bombs hidden around Dushanbe unless their demands were met by two p.m. (0900 GMT) on Sunday.

The hostage-takers call themselves "Rizvon Sadirov's Group" and said they were loyal to Sadirov, a rebel leader who changed sides last month to back the government but apparently remains defiant of Dushanbe's authority.

They demanded the rebels free Sadirov's brother, who is held by opposition fighters in the mountainous Tavildara region. Sadirov himself is believed to be in Afghanistan with groups of armed followers.
